correctness.rationale: For every \(1<\alpha\le2\) and \(u,v>0\), with exactly zero initial derivative, \(A^2=-(u+v)A\) gives \(P=\Pi+f(I-\Pi)\), reducing all-time entrywise positivity to two exact diagonal inequalities. For \(1<\alpha<2\), the normalized positive Fourier density of \(f(s)=E_\alpha(-|s|^\alpha)\) proves \(-1<f(s)\le1\), while the classical large-negative-argument asymptotic proves a negative attained minimum. These facts give the sharp rate interval with equality attained. Scheffé convergence and the scalar power series yield both endpoint limits. The determinant equals the negative-valued scalar mode at some finite time, contradicting the strictly positive determinant of any time-varying Markov fundamental solution with locally integrable finite jump rates. The checker tests examples only; analytical identities prove the infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: The recent finite-state compatibility question for higher-order fractional dynamics naturally demands a minimal two-state test. The result supplies a complete all-time phase diagram for every positive pair of jump rates, a nonempty exceptional probability-matrix region when \(1<\alpha<2\), and its sharp collapse as \(\alpha\uparrow2\), distinguishing scalar positivity from the stronger Markov-generator constraint. This is a complete motivated classification, not a routine normalization check or an arbitrary numerical slice.
